items.title: Pag e 9 HOUSING AFFORDABILITY IMPACT STATEMENT Ci ty of St. Petersburg Housing Affordability Impact Statement Ea ch year, the City of St. Petersburg receives approximately $2 million in State Housing Initiative Partnership (SHIP) funds for its affordable housing programs. To receive these funds, the City is required to maintain an ongoing process for review of local policies, ordinances, resolutions, and plan provisions that increase the cost of housing construction, or of housing redevelopment, and to establish a tracking system to estimate the cumulative cost per housing unit from these actions for the period July 1– June 30 annually. This form should be attached to all policies, ordinances, resolutions, and plan provisions which increase housing costs, and a copy of the completed form should be provided to the City’s Housing and Community Development Department.

items.title: 04 | MANAGEMENT, OPERATIONS, + GOVERNANCE TRAILS CROSSING MASTER PLAN 103102 CONCEPTUAL REVENUE ANALYSIS Achieving full ﬁ nancial self-sustainability at Trails Crossing will be challenging. While the City may play a role in supporting capital improvements, grants, and other funding opportunities, the extent of that participation has not yet been established. A comprehensive and diversiﬁ ed ﬁ nancial strategy will therefore be needed to supplement earned revenue and support long-term operations and maintenance. ENTERPRISE MODEL VIABILITY AND REVENUE DIVERSITY At the St. Petersburg Pier, the enterprise facility generates signiﬁ cant annual revenue – approximately $1.5 million – through tenant leases and events. However, even with this substantial income, the Pier still relies on city subsidies for the remainder of its funding. Because of the unique constraints of Trails Crossing, an enterprise funding model – whereby the cultural linear park would operate like a self-sustaining private business – is currently not recommended. A healthy balance of leases, events, sponsorships, and city support is key to ensuring ﬁ nancial stability and resilience, particularly during disruptions. PHIL

items.title: TRAILS CROSSING MASTER PLAN 107106 OPERATING AND MANAGEMENT MODEL ALTERNATIVES 04 | MANAGEMENT, OPERATIONS, + GOVERNANCE ADVANTAGES: • Municipal Support Frameworks: The City already has precedents for assisting these districts by funding their Executive Directors and limited physical components, such as banners. • Community Activation: These districts successfully organize volunteer street clean-ups and produce local events, fostering grassroots community engagement. CHALLENGES: • Financial Instability: The lack of a compulsory funding mechanism makes these Main Street organizations inherently ﬁ nancially unstable. • Inadequate Maintenance: They do not utilize professional contracted cleaning services, relying instead on volunteers to keep areas clean. This is likely insuffi cient for the rigorous daily maintenance required at a major cultural linear park. • Mismatched Scope: These districts are not designed to manage traditional parks or complex open spaces.
